description:
MODIS ve VIIRS uydu yangın verilerini birleştirip bölge ve tarih seçilebilen bir yangın takvimi web uygulaması geliştiriyoruz.

EN: We are building a MODIS + VIIRS fire hotspot calendar web app.
summary: Burn Calendar is a web calendar that shows every month of NASA FIRMS fire detections since July 2002 on one consistent scale. MODIS (since 2002) and VIIRS (since 2012) detect fires differently, so raw counts jump at the sensor change. We remove static sources, sea and low-confidence detections, then convert MODIS counts to VIIRS equivalents with monthly coefficients computed per region from 2012–2022, when both sensors overlap. We tested the method on 2023–2025, years the coefficients never saw: for Türkiye the annual error averages 4.6% and the 2023–2025 total is within 1.5%. The raw VIIRS/MODIS ratio differs by region (3.25 in Türkiye, 7.07 in the Eastern Mediterranean), so seven regions are calibrated separately and the less certain ones are labelled experimental. Users compare any month with its history, draw their own area, play the years on a map, share a link and download CSV. The site is keyboard accessible, uses colour-blind-safe scales and works in English and Turkish.
details:
What it does: Burn Calendar answers "is this month unusual?" for wildfires. It shows monthly fire detections for each month since July 2002 as a calendar, compared with the same month in all other years, with key findings, a map layer, yearly totals, CSV download and a shareable link.

How it works: MODIS Collection 6.1 (from 2002) and VIIRS S-NPP (from 2012) count fires differently, so raw series break at 2012. For each region we filter static sources, sea and low-confidence detections, then convert MODIS to VIIRS-equivalent counts using monthly coefficients computed from 2012–2022, with outage days removed. NOAA-20 is added with a measured adjustment factor. We validated on 2023–2025, which the coefficients never used. Raw VIIRS/MODIS ratios differ by region (Türkiye 3.25, Balkans 3.65, Caucasus 3.87, Eastern Mediterranean 7.07, SE Australia 5.12, California 4.30, Amazon arc 3.84), so we calibrate each of the seven regions separately and label regions with larger errors as experimental. Estimated months are marked on the calendar and in the charts. NASA POWER temperature and precipitation are shown alongside, not as a causal claim.

Impact: A consistent baseline lets communities, students and analysts judge whether a season is unusual without false jumps from the 2012 sensor change, with clear uncertainty labels.

Tools: Python (data processing), static HTML/JavaScript/CSS, Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for the map, GitHub Pages for hosting. Full method: https://github.com/meceylan/yolcular/blob/main/docs/method.md Code: https://github.com/meceylan/yolcular

Creativity and design: calendar view with hatched estimates, a colour-blind-safe inferno scale, keyboard navigation, English and Turkish interface.

Super Intelligence (SI) use: Claude (Anthropic) was used for planning, writing code, processing data, and drafting documentation and translations. Our team defined the approach, chose the validation design, and reviewed results against the data. This is also stated in the website footer and README.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20 active fire data)
